description:
Draw a selectable, grounded card over one or more already-resolved records — their neighborhood graph plus a written summary of what they have in common (or, for a single record, a rich description of it).

Use this for an open-ended "tell me about X" / "tell me everything about X" / "show me all you got on X" / "what do you have on X" ask about one or more already-identified entities, even for ONE record, or a "pick a few Y to do Z with" ask where the user wants a selectable set of candidates rather than a flat list. Only a narrow, specific question about one entity ("does X pay on time?") goes to well_describe_entity instead. Resolve the record id(s) first (well_get_entity or well_query_records), then call this tool with that root + those ids — never a guessed id or a name string.

Always pass invocation_context with the reason this view is being drawn, even a plain one.

The card renders the graph and the written prose itself — this tool's text result reports only the counts, so say what the selection is rather than repeating the summary.

Call well_wait_for_selection with kind "record_graph_pick" right after this, in the same turn, to hold the turn open for the card's Continue click. On "selected", act on selection.record_graph directly — never guess what the user picked.

This tool reads only — it changes nothing.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

invocation_context.description: A short note on WHY this selection is being summarized (e.g. "companies late on their bills, to draft a collections message"). Flows into the writer so its prose can explain why these records fit — never a source of facts or numbers, only the graph and metrics ground those.

record_ids.description: The exact record ids to build the view for. Resolve X to its id first (well_get_entity or well_query_records) — never a guessed id or a name string.

root.description: Which records root the ids resolve on, e.g. companies | people | invoices.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

name: well_show_record_graph_summary

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

node_count.description: Nodes the server resolved into the selection's neighborhood graph.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

title: Show record graph summary
